pages.x: For years Israel and Iran had fought in the shadows, with killings, cyber attacks and armed allies. Iran was enriching uranium to 60 per cent, close to the level for a bomb, though it said its programme was peaceful. In 2024 the two struck each other openly, and on 12 June 2025 the UN's nuclear watchdog found Iran in breach of its duties.

Before dawn on 13 June Israeli jets, and drones that Israel said its agents had smuggled into Iran, struck air defences, missile launchers and the enrichment plant at Natanz. Strikes in Tehran killed the head of the armed forces, the commander of the Revolutionary Guards and several nuclear scientists. Israel said it was acting to stop Iran building a bomb. Iran denied seeking one.

That night Iran began firing waves of ballistic missiles and drones at Israel. Over twelve days it launched hundreds of missiles and about a thousand drones. Most were shot down, but missiles struck homes in Tel Aviv, Bat Yam and other towns, the oil refinery at Haifa and a hospital in Beersheba, and Israelis spent their nights in shelters.

Israel's air force won control of the skies over western Iran and Tehran, and widened its attacks to missile bases, the nuclear site at Isfahan, fuel depots, military and police headquarters and the state broadcaster, hit during a live news programme. Many people fled Tehran.

On 22 June the United States joined in. B-2 bombers flew from Missouri and dropped fourteen huge bunker-busting bombs on the enrichment plant buried inside a mountain at Fordow and on Natanz, while a submarine fired missiles at Isfahan. President Trump said the sites had been obliterated. Later assessments of the damage differed.

On 23 June Iran fired missiles at the American air base at Al Udeid in Qatar, after giving warning, and almost all were shot down without casualties. Hours later President Trump announced a ceasefire. After a last exchange of strikes, it took hold on 24 June. Both Israel and Iran claimed victory.

Iranian officials said about 1,000 people had been killed in Iran, among them commanders, scientists and many civilians. In Israel about 30 people were killed, almost all of them civilians. In both countries thousands were wounded or lost their homes.
pages.of: killed in Iran, by its own count

pages.x: How far Iran's nuclear programme had been set back stayed in dispute, and no one could be sure what had become of its enriched uranium. Iran cut back its work with UN inspectors, and in September 2025 United Nations sanctions on Iran were restored at the request of Britain, France and Germany.
